name: Conclusion

global_influences.evidence: Band members unanimously credited Owned as their key inspiration, indicating a primarily domestic (rather than Western) lineage of influence — an example of intra-scene Bangladeshi alternative-rock genealogy rather than direct Western import.
global_influences.source: The Business Standard — A fitting 'Conclusion': The band comes full circle

local_adaptation_notes: Conclusion's debut album Mohakashchari (Space Travellers) built the band's identity around melodic alternative and experimental rock combined with a 'rock punch,' gaining recognition among urban youth during a documented mid-2000s to mid-2010s revival of the Bangladeshi rock scene; the band's explicit citation of a domestic band (Owned) as its primary influence — rather than a Western act — is notable evidence of a maturing, self-referential local alternative-rock lineage.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period: emerged during a broadly documented five-to-seven-year revival of Bangladeshi rock (as referenced in retrospective coverage), releasing the widely popular debut album Mohakashchari alongside scattered singles. Line-up transition: original vocalist Atif Imtiaz departed for personal reasons, a significant change for the band's identity. Later period: band marked its 15th year with a reunion solo show bringing together past and present members, indicating a legacy-oriented late-career phase.
concert_culture_notes: Held a celebratory reunion solo show marking the band's 15th anniversary, reuniting past and present members — indicative of a dedicated, multi-generational fan base willing to support legacy-act live events.
listener_community_notes: Frequently discussed as a defining act of the mid-2000s Bangladeshi rock revival among urban youth and young listeners, positioned within the Alternative/Indie genre grouping in the BMEM framework alongside Meghdol and Ashes.
